arxiv-1804-06646.title: Symmetries of free massless particles and soft theorems
arxiv-1804-06646.creator: Shamik Banerjee
arxiv-1804-06646.description: Abstract In an earlier paper we have constructed a basis of massless single particle quantum states which transform in the unitary principal series representation of the four dimensional Lorentz group. The S-matrix written in this basis gives rise to the Mellin transformed amplitude of Pasterski-Shao-Strominger and its generalization.

arxiv-2209-03993.title: Q-learning Decision Transformer: Leveraging Dynamic Programming for Conditional Sequence Modelling in Offline RL
arxiv-2209-03993.creator: Taku Yamagata, Ahmed Khalil, Raúl Santos-Rodríguez
arxiv-2209-03993.description: Abstract Recent works have shown that tackling offline reinforcement learning (RL) with a conditional policy produces promising results. The Decision Transformer (DT) combines the conditional policy approach and a transformer architecture, showing competitive performance against several benchmarks. However, DT lacks stitching ability – one of the critical abilities for offline RL to learn the optimal policy from sub-optimal trajectories.

arxiv-2307-04858.title: AmadeusGPT: a natural language interface for interactive animal behavioral analysis
arxiv-2307-04858.creator: Shaokai Ye, Jessy Lauer, Mu Zhou, Alexander Mathis, Mackenzie W. Mathis
arxiv-2307-04858.description: Abstract The process of quantifying and analyzing animal behavior involves translating the naturally occurring descriptive language of their actions into machine-readable code. Yet, codifying behavior analysis is often challenging without deep understanding of animal behavior and technical machine learning knowledge.

arxiv-2311-16838.title: Increasing Transparency of Reinforcement Learning using Shielding for Human Preferences and Explanations
arxiv-2311-16838.creator: Georgios Angelopoulos, Luigi Mangiacapra, Alessandra Rossi, Claudia Di Napoli, Silvia Rossi
arxiv-2311-16838.description: Abstract The adoption of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in several human-centred applications provides robots with autonomous decision-making capabilities and adaptability based on the observations of the operating environment. In such scenarios, however, the learning process can make robots’ behaviours unclear and unpredictable to humans, thus preventing a smooth and effective Human-Robot Interaction (HRI).

arxiv-2412-05108.title: Constructing optimal treatment length strategies to maximize quality-adjusted lifetimes Thanks: The authors gratefully acknowledge R01DA058996, R01DA048764, R61NS120240, and R33NS120240 from the National Institutes of Health
arxiv-2412-05108.creator: Hao Sun, Didi Chuxing Technology Company, Department of Biostatistics, Computational Biology, University of Rochester, Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
arxiv-2412-05108.description: Abstract Real-world clinical decision making is a complex process that involves balancing the risks and benefits of treatments. Quality-adjusted lifetime is a composite outcome that combines patient quantity and quality of life, making it an attractive outcome in clinical research. We propose methods for constructing optimal treatment length strategies to maximize this outcome.

arxiv-2504-13532.title: Quantum Walks–Based Adaptive Distribution Generation with Efficient CUDA-Q Acceleration
arxiv-2504-13532.creator: Yen Jui Chang, Wei-Ting Wang, Chen-Yu Liu, Yun-Yuan Wang, Ching-Ray Chang
arxiv-2504-13532.description: Abstract We present a novel Adaptive Distribution Generator (ADG) that leverages a quantum walks–based approach to generate high precision and efficiency of target probability distributions. Our method integrates variational quantum circuits with discrete-time quantum walks(DTQWs)—specifically, split-step quantum walks(SSQWs) and their entangled extensions—to dynamically tune coin parameters and drive the evolution of quantum states towards desired distributions.

arxiv-2505-18929.title: Meta-aware Learning in text-to-SQL Large Language Model*
arxiv-2505-18929.creator: Wenda Zhang
arxiv-2505-18929.description: Abstract The advancements of Large language models (LLMs) have provided great opportunities to text-to-SQL tasks to overcome the main challenges to understand complex domain information and complex database structures in business applications. In this paper, we propose a meta-aware learning framework to integrate domain knowledge, database schema, chain-of-thought reasoning processes, and metadata relationships to improve the SQL generation quality.

arxiv-2508-09759.title: Echoes of Agreement: Argument Driven Opinion Shifts in Large Language Models
arxiv-2508-09759.creator: Avneet Kaur
arxiv-2508-09759.description: Abstract There have been numerous studies evaluating bias of LLMs towards political topics. However, how positions towards these topics reflect in model outputs are highly sensitive to the prompt. What happens when the prompt itself is suggestive of certain arguments towards those positions remains underexplored.

arxiv-2510-20704.title: Shear viscosity of a binary mixture for a relativistic fluid at high temperature
arxiv-2510-20704.creator: Gabriele Parisi, Vincenzo Nugara, Salvatore Plumari, Vincenzo Greco
arxiv-2510-20704.description: Abstract The determination of the shear viscosity is a central topic in various areas of modern physics. In particular, it is often necessary to evaluate the shear viscosity η \eta of fluids made up of more than one species, all interacting with different cross sections.

arxiv-2512-01516.title: On the Morrison-Kawamata dream space and its applications
arxiv-2512-01516.creator: Sung Rak Choi, Xingying Li, Zhan Li, Chuyu Zhou
arxiv-2512-01516.description: Abstract . We develop the theory of Morrison-Kawamata dream spaces, which axiomatizes varieties (not necessarily of Calabi-Yau type) that satisfy the Morrison–Kawamata cone conjecture. Using this theory, we establish the generic deformation invariance of various cones and apply it to the boundedness problem of algebraic varieties. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 14J45, 14E30 1.

pmc-10716409.title: Level I of evidence does not support manual lymphatic drainage for total knee arthroplasty: a meta-analysis
pmc-10716409.creator: Filippo Migliorini, Luise Schäfer, Francesca Alzira Bertini, Michael Kurt Memminger, Francesco Simeone, Riccardo Giorgino, Nicola Maffulli
pmc-10716409.description: It is unclear whether manual lymphatic drainage (MLD) following primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is effective in reducing pain and swelling and improving knee function. The present study investigated the efficacy of MLD after TKA. The outcomes of interest are the range of motion (ROM), pain (visual analogue scale, VAS), and circumference of the lower leg.

pmc-10720549.description: The whole genome sequence of Streptomyces sp. strain VNUA74, isolated from soil in a banana farm in Vietnam and exhibited fungicidal effects on banana Colletotrichum spp., was sequenced by PacBio RS II and DNBseq sequencing platforms. The complete circular genome is 7,250,076 bp with a GC content of 72.69%. ANNOUNCEMENT The Streptomyces sp.

pmc-11600242.title: A Micromanipulation‐Actuated Large‐Scale Screening to Identify Optimized Microphysiological Model Parameters in Skeletal Muscle Regeneration (Adv. Sci. 44/2024)
pmc-11600242.creator: Xie Chen, Tao Sun, Shingo Shimoda, Huaping Wang, Qiang Huang, Toshio Fukuda, Qing Shi
pmc-11600242.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Robotic Screening for Muscle Regeneration In article number 2403622, Tao Sun, Qing Shi, and colleagues present a robotic micromanipulation approach to assess the regeneration quality of engineered muscle microfibers by measuring their viscoelasticity and contractile force. This method, which leverages micro‐scale sample volumes, high precision, and automated robotic manipulation, enables large‐scale screening to optimize muscle microphysiological models in complex skeletal muscle regeneration. The concept draws inspiration from the Chinese myth of “Phoenix Nirvana,” symbolizing the challenge of achieving successful muscle regeneration.

pmc-11688075.title: Prescription regularity and pharmacodynamics mechanism of traditional Chinese medicine in autoimmune hepatitis: A data mining and network pharmacology study
pmc-11688075.creator: Di Guo, Xin Li, Shiya Wei, Fenqing Cai, Yang Liu
pmc-11688075.description: This study aims to provide a basis and reference for traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in treating autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) by exploring the prescription patterns of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in treating autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) and predicting the potential mechanisms of core TCM formula.

pmc-11711980.title: GEAR 2.0 ‐ Detection of Dementia and Cognitive Impairment
pmc-11711980.creator: Ula Hwang
pmc-11711980.description: Older adults use the emergency department (ED) as an important source of acute medical care, making 20+ million visits annually. Persons living with dementia are twice as likely to use the ED and 1.5 times more likely to have an avoidable visit.

pmc-11758789.title: RNA-TorsionBERT: leveraging language models for RNA 3D torsion angles prediction
pmc-11758789.creator: Clément Bernard, Guillaume Postic, Sahar Ghannay, Fariza Tahi, Jianlin Cheng
pmc-11758789.description: MotivationPredicting the 3D structure of RNA is an ongoing challenge that has yet to be completely addressed despite continuous advancements. RNA 3D structures rely on distances between residues and base interactions but also backbone torsional angles. Knowing the torsional angles for each residue could help reconstruct its global folding, which is what we tackle in this work.

pmc-13145141.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1892 ACUTE ISCHAEMIC STROKE AND THROMBOLYSIS IN THE CONTEXT OF SEVERE ANAEMIA OF UNDETERMINED CAUSE: A RARE CASE PRESENTATION
pmc-13145141.creator: Shahbaz Alam Khan, Jahanzeb Rehan
pmc-13145141.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and aimsIntravenous thrombolysis is an established treatment for acute ischaemic stroke, with strict eligibility criteria. Current international guidelines define contraindications based on active bleeding and coagulopathy but do not specify a haemoglobin threshold. Nevertheless, observational evidence shows that anaemia predicts poorer outcomes after thrombolysis and severe anaemia often raises clinical concern and may complicate decision-making, particularly when its cause is unclear.

pmc-13342227.title: Method for AFM investigation of lateral forces required for the surface detachment of neurites
pmc-13342227.creator: Vinzent Braemer, Gerrit Paasche
pmc-13342227.description: Resprouting of neurites to establish direct connections between stimulation electrodes and spiral ganglion neurons is of considerable interest in current cochlear implant research. The adhesion strength of neurites to implant surfaces is a critical factor determining whether such connections develop, remain stable or are disrupted shortly after formation.

pmc-13345693.title: MAM‐Localized MANF Counteracts Microinflammatory Stress to Attenuate Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Cataractogenesis in High Myopia
pmc-13345693.creator: Xin Liu, Hao Li, Ching Kang, Dongling Guo, Shuyu Liu, Jiaqi Meng, Zhiqian Huang, Yu Du, Xiangjia Zhu
pmc-13345693.description: Chronic microinflammation drives tissue degeneration, particularly in age‐related and metabolic diseases, yet how it disrupts inter‐organelle communication that leads to cellular failure remains largely unexplored. Utilizing highly myopic cataract (HMC) as a paradigm, we uncover a non‐canonical defense mechanism centered on mitochondria‐associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes (MAMs).

pmc-13594536.title: Neuromelioidosis presenting with the 'tunnel sign': A case report
pmc-13594536.creator: Kamani Naresh Babu, M Keerthi, K Sai Kiran, M Narendhar
pmc-13594536.description: A 31 yr old male came with complaints of fever of 2 weeks duration with headache. Later he developed right hemiparesis with dysarthria followed by left hemiparesis with anarthria. On examination there was spastic quadriparesis. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain contrast showed multiple ring-enhancing lesions of 2–4 cm size in bilateral cerebral hemispheres with central diffusion restriction.
